reason: The cited evidence (E1–E3) demonstrates that a Ti/Ni coating on diamond particles, processed by SPS, forms a TiC layer that improves bonding, density, and mechanical properties in an HEA/diamond composite. However, the evidence does not involve tungsten, copper, or the TiW2 intermetallic, nor does it address thermal conductivity or irradiation resistance. Thus, the key premises specific to the W–Cu system and TiW2 formation are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: A thin Ti coating on particles can react during SPS to form an intermetallic or carbide layer that improves interfacial bonding.
Such a reaction layer reduces interfacial energy, promotes wetting, and eliminates voids.
Improved interfacial bonding and reduced voids lead to enhanced thermal conductivity and mechanical durability.
The specific intermetallic formed will be TiW2 under the stated SPS conditions.
These benefits will be realized in a W–Cu composite for fusion-reactor joints under irradiation.
